title: Learn, don't copy
recap: Pipo Code explained the seasons with an orange and a lamp.
funFact: Coding agents can turn data into graphics. Next, Pipo Code turns your class survey into a chart!
postcard: an orange circling a glowing lamp on a desk, Pipo pointing and Kai smiling: {answer}
situation: Homework time! What are you working on?
facts: 📚 Homework: why do we have seasons?
🍊 You like examples with an orange and a lamp
systemPrompt: You are Pipo Code, a friendly coding helper on a 10-year-old's laptop. Help with what they ask, in simple words. When you explain something, use short steps.

slots.label: What do you want Pipo Code to do?

pieces.label: Explain why we have seasons
pieces.text: Explain why we have seasons, so I can write my own answer.

pieces.label: Write my homework answer for me
pieces.text: Write my homework answer for me.

slots.label: What does Pipo Code need to know?

pieces.label: Use an orange and a lamp
pieces.text: Explain it with an orange and a lamp.

pieces.label: Ask me a question at the end
pieces.text: Ask me a question at the end to check I get it.

pieces.label: Use big science words to impress my teacher
pieces.text: Use big science words to impress my teacher.
pieces.tip: Words you don't understand won't impress your teacher. Simple words you can explain will.

flaws.hint: You didn't tell Pipo Code what kind of example you like.
flaws.explain: Pipo Code didn't know you like the orange and lamp, so the example is harder to picture.

flaws.hint: You didn't tell Pipo Code how old you are.
flaws.explain: Pipo Code didn't know you're 10, so it used big science words.

signals: (^|\n)[^\n]*\b(we have seasons because|the seasons happen because|seasons are caused by)\b
flaws.hint: Asking Pipo Code to write your answer means you don't learn it.
flaws.explain: Pipo Code wrote the answer for you to copy, so you didn't do the thinking.

lesson: Use Pipo Code to understand, not to copy. Ask for simple words and an example you like.
